content.rendered:
Who We Are

Situated on the unceded territories of the Skwxwú7mesh, Tsleil-Waututh, and xwməθkwəýəm Nations, The Polygon Gallery is a vibrant art institution that inspires and provokes cultural insight through adventurous programming. The Gallery is committed to championing artists and cultivating engaged audiences. Its lens of inquiry creatively responds to shifting perceptions of the world, through the histories and evolving technologies of photography and related media.

Operating as Presentation House Gallery for forty years, the organization has produced over 300 exhibitions and numerous publications, earning a reputation as an adventurous public art institution. The Polygon’s expansive programming has featured acclaimed Vancouver photographers, world‐renowned as well as emerging artists, and innovative exhibitions of historic and vernacular photography.

The Polygon is committed to the development of lens-based practices and to creating pathways for new voices within the medium, particularly as it works to articulate new narratives from artists traditionally outside the Eurocentric perspective of many art galleries. Importantly, The Polygon prioritizes the presentation of work by artists who reflect the diversity of its community. Of primary importance, the Gallery continues to expand its engagement with Indigenous communities, particularly the Squamish and Tsleil-Waututh Nations.

The Polygon is committed to inclusivity, believing that art should be accessible to all people. To this end, The Polygon has removed financial barriers to participation: admission to The Polygon is offered on a by-donation basis (all day, every day), with exhibition tours, talks, and outreach programs all included. Additionally, the Gallery is working to expand its audience by providing exhibition tours in English, Farsi, French, Mandarin, and Spanish.

The Polygon is focused on providing a fun and welcoming environment for children and families, so that people from an early age come to know The Polygon as their place for interacting with, and learning about, art. This includes programs such as Gallery School, Chester Fields, Kids First Saturdays, and ongoing self-guided activities that help adults to enjoy visits with their children, all of which are free or included with admission-by-donation.

A Landmark Designed by Local Architects

The Polygon Gallery is a place for art and an incubator for new ideas. Award‐winning firm Patkau Architects envisioned the design as a response to the history and character of both the gallery and its new location at the Shipyards on Lower Lonsdale: “It is an historically resonant site — home to the port industries on which North Vancouver was built, where the mountains meet the sea.”

The Polygon Gallery’s distinctive architecture is prominent along the North Vancouver harbourfront, appearing as a singular, cohesive form. It’s reflective cladding, animated by the changing light of day, echoes the nature of the surrounding landscape. The main floor’s glass exterior invites the public to not only look inside but to see through the gallery. Conversely, the upper floor maintains an enclosed gallery space.

Acknowledgements

The Polygon Gallery is a public cultural facility operated by the British Columbia Photography and Media Arts Society, a federally registered charity. It is grateful for the ongoing support of the Canada Council for the Arts, the British Columbia Arts Council, the Province of British Columbia, and the City of North Vancouver and the District of North Vancouver through the North Vancouver Recreation & Culture Commission.

Address

101 Carrie Cates Court
North Vancouver, BC,V7M 3J4
Unceded territories of the sḵwx̱wú7mesh (Squamish) and səl̓ílwətaʔɬ (Tsleil-Waututh) Nations, and the xʷməθkʷəy̓əm (Musqueam) Band

Gallery Hours

Monday + Tuesday: Closed
Wednesday: 10:00am – 5:00pm
Thursday: 10:00am – 9:00pm
Friday: 10:00am – 5:00pm
Saturday: 10:00am – 5:00pm
Sunday: 10:00am – 5:00pm

Admission

Admission to The Polygon Gallery is by donation, made possible through generous, multi-year support from BMO Financial Group.

Getting Here

The Polygon Gallery is located at the bottom of Lonsdale Avenue, between the Tap & Barrel and Lonsdale Quay, 700 meters east of the Lonsdale Quay SeaBus Terminal. The main entrance is on the east side of the building, opposite the Tap & Barrel.

Accessibility

The Polygon is wheelchair accessible, with accessible washrooms on the ground floor and baby changing facilities on both floors.

There is wheelchair accessible parking underneath Lonsdale Quay Market, approximately 150 metres from the Gallery’s entrance.

There is a loading zone for drop-offs along Carrie Cates Court, approximately 40 metres from the Gallery’s entrance.

Automatic door openers are installed at the entrance and on all doors leading to exhibition and program spaces inside the building.

The Gallery has a wheelchair for use during your visit.

There is an elevator to access to the upstairs gallery, around the corner from the Admissions desk.

Assistance dogs are welcome. A water bowl is available on request.

Please ask our staff if you require any assistance or have any questions.

Gallery Guidelines

No backpacks or large personal items are permitted in the exhibition spaces. There are complimentary lockers on site for temporary storage.

Wet umbrellas should be left in the available umbrella stands at our front entrance.

No food or beverage in the exhibition spaces.

No touching the artwork or pointing closely.

No pens or markers are permitted in the exhibition spaces.

Parking

One-hour street parking is available surrounding the Gallery. Pay parking is available at Lonsdale Quay Market, the Pinnacle Hotel at the Pier, and the ICBC parkade, located adjacent to Lonsdale Quay Market with entries off Rogers Avenue and Carrie Cates. Chartered buses may temporarily stop and drop guests off in the passenger zone outside The Polygon on Carrie Cates Court. Chartered boats may arrange moorage to St Roch Dock (100 ft. long) located in close proximity to The Polygon. To learn more about this public amenity, contact the City’s Shipyards Liaison at bookings@cnv.org or (604) 982-3910.

Public Transport

The most convenient way to visit The Polygon from downtown Vancouver is via the SeaBus, a 12-minute ride to the North Shore waterfront. The Lonsdale Quay SeaBus Terminal is located approximately 700 metres west from the Gallery’s main entrance. In addition to the SeaBus, it offers bus service for the R2, 228, 229, 230, 231, 236, 249, N24 routes. There are numerous rest areas between the SeaBus Terminal and The Polygon Gallery.

Plan your transit ride, visit: translink.ca

Image: Akeem Nermo

Press

For all media enquiries, email Michael at m.mann@thepolygon.ca or call at +1 604 771 6266.

Submissions

The Polygon Gallery exhibits contemporary and historical photography and media art.

Read Submissions Policy

Submissions Policy

The Polygon Gallery does not program exhibitions through submission. However, it welcomes artists and curators who wish to update The Polygon about their work. 

Please be advised, The Polygon cannot take responsibility for the return of submitted material unless accompanied by a self-addressed stamped envelope. Do not send original artwork, and if sending documentation on CD, please include examples in hard copy format.

Please include the following:

  • An up-to-date curriculum vitae

  • A short statement about your work

  • Detailed documentation about each piece

Return Postage

Please include a self-addressed, stamped envelope. Please note that proposals with neither sufficient return postage, nor arrangements for pick-up, will not be returned.

If you are sending material from outside of Canada, please note that the postage must be Canadian. Alternatives are international postage coupons, or money orders. You may consider sending your material electronically instead.

Mail to:

101 Carrie Cates Court
North Vancouver BC Canada
V7M3J4

content.rendered:
DONATE

Art has a wonderful way of connecting people, and The Polygon aims to provide access to art experiences for all members of our community. Every dollar donated helps to support artists, exhibitions, talks, family programs, and more, both within the Gallery’s walls and beyond.

One-time donations of $20 or more are eligible for a full tax receipt. Or consider becoming a Member (starting at $100 annually or $10 per month) and receive a full tax receipt PLUS year-round benefits.

For a deeper commitment, join the Leadership Circle (starting at $1,000 annually or $84 per month).

Thank you for your support!

Donate Now

The British Columbia Photography and Media Arts Society
Charitable Registration No. 896593498 RR 0001

Image: Anita Bonnarens Photography

content.rendered:
Corporate Giving

The Polygon’s corporate donors are committed to providing access to powerful art experiences. Your contribution today will support the upcoming year of exhibitions and education programs that bring art and people of all ages together for the benefit of our community.

Membership starts at $500, and provides companies with exclusive access to The Polygon’s Venue Rentals program for hosting unique client-focused events or company parties.

Join or renew today to enjoy:

  • A tax receipt for the full amount of your contribution
  • UNLIMITED admissions for all employees and a guest on every visit
  • Access to The Polygon’s Venue Rentals program for hosting private events
  • Invitations to exclusive Member events hosted at The Polygon
  • Invitations to attend annual Corporate Member Days offering all employees and their families free admission to exhibitions and public programs
  • 10% discount in The Polygon Shop and Bookstore (excluding sale merchandise)
Join or Renew Now

The British Columbia Photography and Media Arts Society
Charitable Registration No. 896593498 RR 0001
